questions.q: Which one of the following is correct in respect of the commencement of the election process in India? [1995]
o: (d) Both the exercises of making a recommendation...
(c) The recommendation for election is made by the...
(a) The recommendation for election is made by the...
(b) The recommendation for election is made by the...
questions.e: The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes. The recommendation for election is made by the EC, but the formal notification is issued by the President (for Parliament) and Governors (for State Assemblies).

questions.q: Which of the followings political parties is/are national political parties? 1️⃣ Muslim League 2️⃣ Revolutionary Socialist Party 3️⃣ All India Forward Block 4️⃣ Peasants and Workers Party of India [1995]
questions.e: According to the document, all the parties mentioned in the list (Muslim League, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Block, and Peasants and Workers Party of India) are considered state-level parties rather than national parties.

questions.q: The Dinesh Goswami Committee was concerned with: [1995]
o: (c) steps to put down insurgency in the north-east
questions.e: The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) was specifically concerned with electoral reforms in India. Its recommendations included state funding in kind to political parties and restricting candidates from contesting from more than two constituencies.

questions.q: If in an election to a State legislative assembly, the candidate who is declared elected loses his deposit, it means that: [1995]
o: (d) a very large number of candidates contested the election
(c) the elected candidate's victory over his nearest rival was very marginal
(b) the election was for a multi-member constituency
questions.e: A candidate loses their security deposit if they fail to secure more than one-sixth of the valid votes. In a field with a very large number of candidates, the votes can be so distributed that even the winner fails to reach the 1/6th threshold.

questions.q: Which one of the following will fit in the place marked 'X' in the table regarding the composition of the House of the People? [1995]
o: (d) The Attorney General who has the right to spea...
(c) Not more than 20 representative of Union Terri...
(a) Ministers who are not members of Parliament bu...
questions.e: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha (552) is composed of up to 530 representatives of States, up to 20 representatives of Union Territories, and 2 nominated Anglo-Indians.

questions.q: Who among the following have the right to vote in the elections to both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha? [1995]
o: (b) Elected members of the Upper House of the Parliament
(d) Elected members of the Lower House of the State Legislature
(c) Elected members of the Upper House of the State Legislature
(a) Elected members of the Lower House of the Parliament
questions.e: Elected members of the State Legislative Assembly (MLAs) vote directly for Rajya Sabha representatives. As citizens, they also vote in the general elections for the Lok Sabha under Universal Adult Suffrage.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a part of the electoral college for the President but, not the forum for his impeachment? [1996]
questions.e: Under Article 54, the electoral college for the President includes elected members of the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies. However, Article 61 states that only members of Parliament (LS and RS) participate in the impeachment process.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the duties of Prime Minister is correct? [1996]
o: (a) Is free to choose his minister only from among...
(b) Can choose his cabinet after consulting the Pr...
(d) Has only limited power in the choice of his ca...
(c) Has full discretion in the choice of persons w...
questions.e: The Prime Minister has full discretion to choose his ministers. He can even choose a person who is not a member of either House, provided that person gains membership within six months.

questions.q: Which one of the following States of India does not have a Legislative Council even though the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 provides for it? [1995]
questions.e: At the time of the document's records, only five states had a bicameral legislature: UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Jammu & Kashmir. Madhya Pradesh did not have a Legislative Council despite the provision.

questions.q: Which of the following is the State in which the Lok Ayukta Act includes the Chief Minister in its ambit? [1995]
questions.e: In the states of Gujarat and Maharashtra, the Chief Minister is brought under the jurisdiction and ambit of the Lok Ayukta Act.

questions.q: Of the four forms of political protests mentioned below, which one is derived from the name of the person who used it as a political weapon for the first time? [1995]
questions.e: The term "Boycott" is derived from Captain Charles Cunningham Boycott, a British land agent in Ireland who was ostracized by his community in 1880 as part of an agrarian protest.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): The word minority is not defined in the Constitution of India. Reason (R): The Minorities Commission is not a constitutional body. [1996]
o: (b) Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
(c) A is true but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
(a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.e: While it is true that "minority" is not defined in the Constitution and the Minorities Commission is currently a statutory (not constitutional) body, the status of the Commission does not explain why the term is undefined in the Constitution.

questions.q: If the Prime Minister of India belonged to the Upper House of Parliament: [1997]
o: (b) he will not be able to speak on the budget in the Lower House
(a) he will not be able to vote in his favour in the event of a no-confidence motion
(c) he can make statements only in the Upper House
(d) he was to become a member of the Lower House within six months after being sworn in
questions.e: A no-confidence motion can only be moved and voted upon in the Lok Sabha. If the PM is a member of the Rajya Sabha (Upper House), he cannot vote in the Lok Sabha, even on a motion concerning his own government.

questions.q: In the Presidential election in India, the expression "population" for calculating vote value (as of 1997) means the population as ascertained by the: [1997]
questions.e: For the purpose of Presidential elections, the "population" refers to the data from the 1971 Census to ensure uniformity in representation across states based on older demographic ratios.

questions.q: Match List I (Functionaries) with List II (Oaths) and select the correct answer: 1️⃣ President of India: Faith and Allegiance to the Constitution 2️⃣ Judges of Supreme Court: Upholding the Constitution and the law 3️⃣ Members of Parliament: Faithful Discharge of duties 4️⃣ Minister for the Union: Secrecy of information [1997]
questions.e: The President takes an oath under Article 60 to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution. Other functionaries like SC judges, MPs, and Union Ministers take oaths specified in the Third Schedule, focusing on upholding the law, discharge of duties, and secrecy respectively.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a principle of "Panchsheel"? [1997]
o: (d) Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs
(c) Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty
questions.e: The five principles of Panchsheel (1954) include mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality/mutual benefit, and peaceful co-existence. "Non-alignment" is a movement based on these principles but is not one of the five specific principles.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about a Money Bill is not correct? [2000]
o: (d) The President cannot return a Money Bill to th...
(a) A Money Bill can be tabled in either House of...
(c) The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill passe...
(b) The Speaker of Lok Sabha is the final authorit...
questions.e: According to Article 110, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and it requires the prior recommendation of the President. It cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: The Speaker can ask a member of the House to stop speaking and let another member speak. This phenomenon is known as: [2000]
questions.e: "Yielding the floor" occurs when the Speaker gives a portion of a member's speaking time to another. "Decorum" refers to proper behavior, "interpellation" to formal questioning of the government, and "crossing the floor" to voting against party lines.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India: 1️⃣ He is appointed by the President of India 2️⃣ He must have the same qualifications as are required for a judge of the Supreme Court 3️⃣ He must be a member of either House of Parliament 4️⃣ He can be removed by impeachment by Parliament [2000]
questions.e: The Attorney General is appointed by the President under Article 76 and must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge. He does not need to be a member of Parliament and serves at the pleasure of the President, with no provision for impeachment.

questions.q: The primary function of the Finance Commission in India is to: [2000]
o: (a) distribution of revenue between the Centre and the States
(c) advise the President on financial matters
(d) allocate funds to various ministries of the Union and State Governments
questions.e: Under Article 280, the Finance Commission's duty is to make recommendations to the President regarding the distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States and the allocation of grants-in-aid.

questions.q: The Parliament can make any law for the whole or any part of India for implementing international treaties: [2000]
o: (c) with the consent of the States concerned
(b) with the consent of the majority of States
(a) with the consent of all the State
(d) without the consent of any State
questions.e: Article 253 grants Parliament the sole prerogative to make laws for the entire country or any part thereof to implement international treaties, agreements, or conventions without requiring the consent of the states.

questions.q: The state which has the largest number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha is: [2000]
questions.e: According to the document, Madhya Pradesh has the largest number of seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Consider the following functionaries: 1️⃣ Cabinet Secretary 2️⃣ Chief Election Commissioner 3️⃣ Union Cabinet Minister 4️⃣ Chief Justice of India. Their correct sequence in the Order of Precedence is: [2000]
questions.e: In the official Order of Precedence, the Chief Justice of India ranks highest among the listed, followed by Union Cabinet Ministers, then the Chief Election Commissioner, and finally the Cabinet Secretary.

questions.q: Which one of the following duties is not performed by Comptroller and Auditor General of India? [2001]
o: (b) To audit and report on all expenditure from th...
(a) To audit and report on all expenditure from th...
(d) To control the receipt and issue of public mon...
(c) To audit and report on all trading, manufactur...
questions.e: Article 149 defines the CAG's duties primarily around auditing and reporting on accounts. Unlike the UK's CAG, the Indian CAG does not have the power to control the actual "issue" or withdrawal of money from the exchequer; that is done by the executive.

questions.q: In what way does the Indian Parliament exercise control over the administration? [2001]
o: (d) By compelling the executive to issue writs
(b) Through Consultative Committees in various ministries
(c) By making the administrators send periodic reports
questions.e: Parliament exercises detailed scrutiny and control over the administration through various Parliamentary Committees (Standing and Ad-hoc), which are regulated under Article 118(1).

questions.q: In which one of the following areas does the State Government not have control over its local bodies? [2001]
questions.e: While State governments have significant control over local bodies regarding legislation, finance, and personnel, they do not exercise control in the matter of handling individual citizens' grievances against those bodies.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the political parties in India: 1️⃣ The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for the registration of political parties 2️⃣ Registration of political parties is carried out by the Election Commission 3️⃣ A national level political party is one which is recognized in four or more states 4️⃣ During the 1999 general elections, there were six national and 48 state level parties recognized. [2001]
questions.e: All statements are accurate: the RPA 1951 governs registration via the EC, a national party requires recognition in at least four states, and the 1999 election data matches official records.

questions.q: With reference to Indian polity, which one of the following statements is correct? [2002]
o: (b) President can make ordinance only when either...
(a) Planning Commission is accountable to the Parl...
(d) National Development Council is constituted of...
(c) The minimum age prescribed for appointment as...
questions.e: Under Article 123, the President can only issue ordinances when both Houses are not in session. There is no minimum age for SC judges in the Constitution, and the Planning Commission is not constitutionally accountable to Parliament.

questions.q: Consider the following statements with reference to India: 1️⃣ The Chief Election Commission and other Election Commissioners enjoy equal powers but receive unequal salaries 2️⃣ The Chief Election Commissioner is entitled to the same salary as is provided to a judge of the Supreme Court 3️⃣ The Chief Election Commissioner shall not be removed from his office except in like manner and on like grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court 4️⃣ The term of office of the Election Commissioner is five years. [2002]
questions.e: The CEC and other ECs enjoy equal powers and equal salaries. The CEC’s removal process is identical to that of an SC judge. Their term is 6 years (not 5) or until age 65.

questions.q: In the case of election to the Lok Sabha, the amount of Security deposited for general category candidates (as of 2002) is: [2002]
questions.e: In 2002, the security deposit for a general candidate in a Lok Sabha election was ₹10,000. For SC/ST candidates, it was ₹5,000. (Note: These amounts were updated in later years to ₹25,000 and ₹12,500 respectively).

questions.q: The term of the Lok Sabha: [2002]
o: (b) can be extended by six months at a time
(a) cannot be extended under any circumstances
(d) can be extended for two years at a time during the proclamation of emergency
(c) can be extended by one year at a time during the proclamation of emergency
questions.e: Under Article 352, during a proclamation of national emergency, the term of the Lok Sabha can be extended by Parliament by law for a period not exceeding one year at a time.

questions.q: Which one of the following authorities recommends the principles governing the grants-in-aid of the revenues to the states out of the Consolidated Fund of India? [2002]
questions.e: The Finance Commission is constitutionally mandated to recommend the principles that should govern the grants-in-aid to the states from the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct? [2003]
o: (a) Only the Rajya Sabha and not the Lok Sabha can...
(b) There is a constitutional provision for nomina...
(d) A nominated member can vote both in the Presid...
(c) There is no constitutional bar for a nominated...
questions.e: There is no constitutional restriction preventing a nominated member of either House from being appointed as a Union Minister. Nominated members can vote in Vice-Presidential elections but not Presidential elections.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The joint sitting of the two houses of the Parliament in India is sanctioned under Article 108 of the Constitution 2️⃣ The first joint sitting of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha was held in the year 1961 3️⃣ The second joint sitting was held to pass the Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill. [2003]
questions.e: All statements are correct. Joint sittings occur under Article 108. The first was in 1961 (Dowry Prohibition), and the second was in 1978 (Banking Service Commission Repeal).

questions.q: Which one of the following Bills must be passed by each House of the Indian Parliamentary separately by special majority? [2003]
questions.e: Under Article 368, a Constitution Amendment Bill must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

questions.q: As per Indian Protocol, who among the following ranks highest in the order of precedence? [2003]
o: (c) Governor of a State within his State
questions.e: Within the Order of Precedence, a Governor within their own state ranks higher than the Deputy PM, Former Presidents, and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the function(s) of the Finance commission? 1️⃣ To allow the withdrawal of the money out of the Consolidated Fund of India 2️⃣ To allocate between the States the shares of proceeds of taxes 3️⃣ To consider applications for grants-in-aid from States. [2003]
questions.e: The Finance Commission's primary roles are recommending tax distribution between the Union and States and determining principles for grants-in-aid. It has no role in authorizing withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund; that is a Parliamentary function via Appropriation Bills.

questions.q: In the electoral college for Presidential Election in India, the value of the vote of an elected Member of Parliament (MP) equals: [2003]
o: (c) Total value of votes of all elected MLAs divid...
(b) State Population divided by Number of Elected...
(a) The sum of vote value of elected members of al...
questions.e: The value of an MP's vote is determined by dividing the total value of votes of all elected members of all state legislative assemblies by the total number of elected members of both Houses of Parliament.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Members of the Rajya Sabha are associated with Committees on Public Accounts and Public Undertakings 2️⃣ Members of Committee on Estimates are drawn entirely from the Lok Sabha 3️⃣ The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs works under the overall direction of Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs. [2003]
questions.e: The PAC and PUC include members from both Houses (15 LS, 7 RS). The Estimates Committee consists of 30 members exclusively from the Lok Sabha. The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs assists the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs.

questions.q: Survey of India is under the ministry of: [2003]
questions.e: Set up in 1767, the Survey of India is the oldest scientific department of the Government of India and operates under the Department of Science and Technology.

questions.q: With reference to Indian Parliament, which one of the following is not correct? [2004]
o: (b) No money shall be withdrawn from the Consolida...
(a) The Appropriation Bill must be passed by both...
(c) Finance Bill is required for proposing new tax...
(d) No Money Bill can be introduced except on the...
questions.e: An Appropriation Bill is a Money Bill. In the case of Money Bills, the Rajya Sabha has only recommendatory powers and does not "pass" it in the same sense as an ordinary bill; the bill is deemed passed even if the RS does not approve it.

questions.q: Which of the following is the final authority to give a verdict in case of election disputes? [2004]
questions.e: The High Court is the final authority to adjudicate election disputes. Special election benches may be constituted in High Courts specifically for the disposal of election petitions.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Speaker of Lok Sabha: 1️⃣ Has the power to adjourn the House sine die 2️⃣ On prorogation, it is only the President who can summon the House 3️⃣ Continues in office even after the dissolution of the House until the first meeting of the new House. [2004]
questions.e: The Speaker can adjourn the House, but summoning/prorogation is a Presidential power. Under Article 179/94, the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution but remains until immediately before the first meeting of the new House.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding a no-confidence motion is not correct? [2004]
o: (a) In the Lok Sabha, a no-confidence motion has t...
(d) Rajya Sabha is not empowered to entertain a mo...
(b) In the case of a no-confidence motion in Lok S...
(c) A motion of no-confidence once admitted, has t...
questions.e: There is no requirement in the Rules of Procedure for a no-confidence motion to state the specific grounds for its introduction. It only requires the support of at least 50 members of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: The resolution for removing the Vice-President of India can be moved in the: [2004]
questions.e: Under Article 67(b), a resolution to remove the Vice-President must be initiated in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and then agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: With reference to the Constitution of India, which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched? [2004]
o: (c) Post Office Savings Bank: Union List
questions.e: Stock Exchanges and futures markets are listed under the Union List (Item 90 of the Seventh Schedule), not the Concurrent List.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding planning in India: 1️⃣ The highest deciding body for planning in India is the Planning Commission 2️⃣ The Secretary of the Planning Commission is also the Secretary of National Development Council 3️⃣ Economic and social planning is in the Concurrent List. [2004]
questions.e: The highest decision-making body for planning is the Parliament, followed by the NDC. Economic and social planning is indeed entry 20 in the Concurrent List.

questions.q: Which is the correct chronological order of the following events? 1️⃣ Formation of Haryana state 2️⃣ Fourth general elections 3️⃣ Meghalaya and Tripura become full states 4️⃣ Mysore named as Karnataka state. [2004]
questions.e: Haryana was formed in 1966. The 4th General Elections were held in Feb 1967. Tripura and Meghalaya became states in Jan 1972. Mysore was renamed Karnataka in 1973.

questions.q: Under which one of the Ministries of the Government of India does the Food and Nutrition Board work? [2005]
o: (d) Ministry of Women and Child Development
(b) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.e: The Food and Nutrition Board is a technical support wing under the Child Development Bureau of the Ministry of Women and Child Development. (The options in the original text were noted as incorrect).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Rajya Sabha alone has the power to declare that it would be in national interest for the Parliament to legislate with respect to a matter in the State List 2️⃣ Resolutions approving the proclamation of Emergency are passed only by the Lok Sabha. [2006]
questions.e: Under Article 249, only the Rajya Sabha can authorize Parliament to legislate on State List matters. Emergency proclamations, however, must be approved by both Houses of Parliament, not just the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): The Council of Ministers in the Union of India is collectively responsible both to the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Reason (R): The Members of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha are eligible to be the Ministers of the Union Government. [2007]
o: (d) A is false but R is true
(a) Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
(c) A is true but R is false
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
questions.e: While members of both houses can be ministers (Reason is true), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha (Assertion is false).

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Jawaharlal Nehru is/are correct? 1️⃣ He was in his fourth term as Prime Minister at the time of his death 2️⃣ He represented the Rae Bareilly constituency 3️⃣ The first non-Congress PM assumed office in 1977. [2007]
questions.e: Nehru was in his 4th term when he died in 1964. He represented Phulpur, not Rae Bareilly. Morarji Desai became the first non-Congress PM in 1977.

questions.q: Who was the Speaker of the First Lok Sabha? [2007]
questions.e: G.V. Mavalankar served as the Speaker of the First Lok Sabha from 1952 to 1956.

questions.q: Consider the following statements in respect of financial emergency under Article 360: 1️⃣ A proclamation issued shall cease to operate at the expiration of two months unless approved by both Houses 2️⃣ The President can issue directions for reduction of salaries of Union employees excluding Supreme Court and High Court Judges. [2007]
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the President can indeed reduce the salaries of Supreme Court and High Court judges during a financial emergency.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Chairman of the Committee on Public Accounts is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha 2️⃣ The PAC comprises Members of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and few eminent persons of industry. [2007]
questions.e: The PAC Chairman is appointed by the Speaker from among the members of the Lok Sabha. The committee consists of 15 members from LS and 7 from RS, but it does not include external persons from industry.

questions.q: Who among the following have held the office of the Vice-President of India? 1️⃣ Mohammad Hidayatullah 2️⃣ Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed 3️⃣ Neelam Sanjiva Reddy 4️⃣ Shankar Dayal Sharma [2008]
questions.e: Mohammad Hidayatullah (1979-84) and Shankar Dayal Sharma (1987-92) served as Vice-Presidents. Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy served as Presidents but not as Vice-Presidents.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the State Legislative Assembly: 1️⃣ It shall consist of not more than 450 members 2️⃣ A person must be at least 25 years of age to be qualified for a seat. [2008]
questions.e: Under Article 170, a State Legislative Assembly consists of not more than 500 members (not 450) and not less than 60. The minimum age for membership is 25 years.

questions.q: With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ All Cabinet Ministers shall compulsorily be sitting members of Lok Sabha only 2️⃣ The Union Cabinet Secretariat operates under the direction of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs. [2009]
questions.e: Cabinet ministers can be members of either House. The Cabinet Secretariat is under the direct charge of the Prime Minister, not the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.

questions.q: With reference to Union Government, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Ministries and Departments are created by the Prime Minister on the advice of the Cabinet Secretary 2️⃣ Each ministry is assigned to a Minister by the President on the advice of the PM. [2009]
questions.e: Under the Allocation of Business Rules 1961, the President (not the PM alone) creates ministries on the advice of the PM. The President also assigns ministries to ministers on the PM's advice.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the President 2️⃣ High Courts have original, appellate and advisory jurisdiction at the State level. [2009]
questions.e: The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor, not the President. High Courts possess original and appellate jurisdiction; their original criminal jurisdiction was largely removed by the CrPC 1973.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) was set up during the Prime Ministership of Lal Bahadur Shastri 2️⃣ Members of CAT are drawn from both judicial and administrative streams. [2009]
questions.e: CAT was set up in 1985 during Rajiv Gandhi's tenure, not Shastri's. Its members are indeed recruited from both judicial and administrative backgrounds.

questions.q: With reference to Union Government, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Number of Ministries at the Centre on 15th August 1947 was 18 2️⃣ Number of Ministries at the Centre at present (2009) is 36. [2009]
questions.e: On Independence day in 1947, there were exactly 18 ministries. The number varies over time based on policy needs; it was not fixed at 36 in 2009.

questions.q: With reference to the Consumer Disputes Redressal at district level, which statement is not correct? [2010]
o: (a) A State Government can establish more than one District Forum in a district
(b) One of the members of the District Forum shall be a woman
(c) The District Forum entertains complaints where the value does not exceed fifty lakhs
(d) A complaint may be filed by the State Government as a representative
questions.e: At the time of this question (2010), the District Forum's pecuniary jurisdiction was limited to cases not exceeding twenty lakhs, not fifty lakhs.

questions.q: When the annual Union Budget is not passed by the Lok Sabha: [2011]
o: (b) The Budget is referred to the Rajya Sabha for suggestions
(a) The Budget is modified and presented again
(d) The Prime Minister submits the resignation of Council of Ministers
(c) The Union Finance Minister is asked to resign
questions.e: Failure to pass the budget is equivalent to a loss of confidence in the government. Therefore, the entire Council of Ministers must resign.

questions.q: The authorization for the withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India must come from: [2011]
questions.e: No money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without an Appropriation Act passed by the Parliament.

questions.q: In the Parliament of India, the purpose of an adjournment motion is: [2012]
o: (d) to postpone the proceedings to check inappropriate behaviour
(c) to allow a reduction of specific amount in demand for grant
(b) to let opposition members collect information from the ministers
(a) to allow a discussion on a definite matter of urgent public importance
questions.e: An adjournment motion is an extraordinary device used to draw the House's attention to a specific matter of urgent public importance, interrupting regular business.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Union Territories are not represented in the Rajya Sabha 2️⃣ It is within the purview of the Chief Election Commissioner to adjudicate the election disputes 3️⃣ According to the Constitution, the Parliament consists of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha only. [2012]
questions.e: All statements are incorrect. Delhi and Puducherry have RS seats. Election disputes are adjudicated by Courts (HC/SC), not the CEC. Parliament consists of the President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: Regarding the office of the Lok Sabha Speaker, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He/She holds the office during the pleasure of the President 2️⃣ He/She need not be a member of the House at the time of election 3️⃣ If he/she intends to resign, the letter has to be addressed to the Deputy Speaker. [2012]
questions.e: The Speaker is elected by members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves. The Speaker does not hold office at the President's pleasure but for the life of the House, and resignation is addressed to the Deputy Speaker.

questions.q: Which of the following can be said to be essentially the parts of 'Inclusive Governance'? 1️⃣ Permitting Non-Banking Financial Companies to do banking 2️⃣ Establishing effective District Planning Committees 3️⃣ Increasing spending on public health 4️⃣ Strengthening the Mid-day Meal Scheme. [2012]
questions.e: Inclusive governance aims to reach the downtrodden. Items 2, 3, and 4 directly support this. Permitting NBFCs to do banking is a financial policy but not necessarily a direct component of inclusive governance.

questions.q: Regarding the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), what is its importance? 1️⃣ CAG exercises exchequer control on behalf of Parliament during emergencies 2️⃣ CAG reports on execution of projects are discussed by the PAC 3️⃣ Information from CAG reports can be used by investigating agencies. [2012]
questions.e: The CAG has no exchequer control (control over withdrawals). However, its reports are reviewed by the PAC, and its findings can be used by agencies to frame legal charges for financial violations.

questions.q: The Prime Minister of India, at the time of his/her appointment: [2012]
o: (a) need not necessarily be a member of one of the Houses but must become a member within six months
(b) need not necessarily be a member but must become a member of the Lok Sabha within six months
(d) must be a member of the Lok Sabha
(c) must be a member of one of the Houses
questions.e: Under Article 75, a person can be appointed PM even if not a member of Parliament, provided they are elected to either the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha within six months.

questions.q: A deadlock between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha calls for a joint sitting of the Parliament during the passage of: 1️⃣ Ordinary Legislation 2️⃣ Money Bill 3️⃣ Constitution Amendment Bill. [2012]
questions.e: Joint sittings (Article 108) apply only to Ordinary Bills and Financial Bills. They do not apply to Money Bills (where LS is supreme) or Constitution Amendment Bills.

questions.q: What will follow if a Money Bill is substantially amended by the Rajya Sabha? [2013]
o: (a) The Lok Sabha may still proceed with the Bill, accepting or not accepting the recommendations
(d) The President may call a joint sitting for passing the Bill
(c) The Lok Sabha may send the Bill to the Rajya Sabha for reconsideration
(b) The Lok Sabha cannot consider the bill further
questions.e: The Lok Sabha has the absolute power to accept or reject any recommendations made by the Rajya Sabha regarding a Money Bill.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct? [2013]
o: (a) The same person cannot be appointed as Governor for two or more States
(c) No procedure has been laid down in the Constitution for the removal of a Governor
(b) The Judges of the High Court are appointed by the Governor
(d) The Chief Minister of a Union Territory is appointed by the Lt. Governor
questions.e: The Constitution does not specify a formal procedure or grounds for the removal of a Governor; they serve at the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Attorney General of India can: 1️⃣ take part in the proceedings of the Lok Sabha 2️⃣ be a member of a committee of the Lok Sabha 3️⃣ speak in the Lok Sabha 4️⃣ vote in the Lok Sabha. [2013]
questions.e: The AG has the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of either House and its committees but does not have the right to vote.

questions.q: In the context of India, which of the following principles is/are implied institutionally in the parliamentary government? 1️⃣ Members of the Cabinet are Members of the Parliament 2️⃣ Ministers hold office till they enjoy confidence in the Parliament 3️⃣ Cabinet is headed by the Head of the State. [2013]
questions.e: Cabinet members must be MPs. The government survives only as long as it has parliamentary confidence. However, the Cabinet is headed by the Prime Minister (Head of Government), not the President (Head of State).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Council of Ministers in the Centre shall be collectively responsible to the Parliament 2️⃣ The Union Ministers shall hold the office during the pleasure of the President 3️⃣ The PM shall communicate to the President about proposals for legislation. [2013]
questions.e: Under Article 75, ministers hold office at the President's pleasure. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (not the whole Parliament). Article 78 requires the PM to inform the President of legislative proposals.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are not members of that House 2️⃣ Nominated members of Parliament have no voting right in the presidential election but can vote in the VP election. [2013]
questions.e: The Chairman (VP) is not a member, but the Deputy Chairman is chosen from among the members. Nominated members are excluded from Presidential elections but participate in Vice-Presidential elections.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The President shall make rules for more convenient transaction of business 2️⃣ All executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Prime Minister. [2014]
questions.e: Under Article 77, the President makes rules for business transaction and allocation. However, all executive actions are formally taken in the name of the President, not the Prime Minister.

questions.q: The power to increase the number of judges in the Supreme Court of India is vested in: [2014]
questions.e: Parliament has the exclusive power to increase the number of SC judges. It has done so multiple times, most recently increasing the count to thirty-one in 2008.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding a No-Confidence Motion in India: 1️⃣ There is no mention of a No-Confidence Motion in the Constitution 2️⃣ A Motion of No-Confidence can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only. [2014]
questions.e: The term is not in the Constitution; the procedure originates from Rule 198 of the Lok Sabha Rules. It can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the largest Committee of the Parliament? [2014]
questions.e: The Committee on Estimates is the largest, consisting of 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Which of the following are the discretionary powers given to the Governor of a State? 1️⃣ Sending a report for imposing President's rule 2️⃣ Appointing the Ministers 3️⃣ Reserving certain bills for the President 4️⃣ Making rules to conduct business. [2014]
questions.e: The Governor has constitutional discretion in recommending President's Rule and reserving bills. Minister appointments are done on the advice of the CM, not via independent discretion.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the function/functions of the Cabinet Secretariat? 1️⃣ Preparation of agenda for Cabinet Meetings 2️⃣ Secretarial assistance to Cabinet Committees 3️⃣ Allocation of financial resources to the Ministries. [2014]
questions.e: The Secretariat prepares agendas and provides secretarial support. Resource allocation is the responsibility of the Finance Ministry, not the Cabinet Secretariat.

questions.q: A Constitutional Government is one which: [2014]
o: (c) is based on the will of the legislature
(a) places effective restrictions on individual li...
(b) places effective restrictions on the Authority...
questions.e: A constitutional government is essentially a "limited government" that uses a constitution to restrict state power to protect individual liberties.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Legislative Council of a State can be larger than half of the Legislative Assembly 2️⃣ The Governor of a State nominates the Chairman of Legislative Council. [2015]
questions.e: The Council strength is capped at one-third (not half) of the Assembly. The Chairman is elected by the Council members from among themselves, not nominated by the Governor.

questions.q: With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Department of Revenue is responsible for the preparation of Union Budget 2️⃣ No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund without Parliamentary authorization 3️⃣ All disbursements from Public Account need Parliamentary authorization. [2015]
questions.e: The Department of Economic Affairs (not Revenue) prepares the Budget. Withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund require authorization, but Public Account transactions are executive actions and do not.

questions.q: There is a Parliamentary System of Government in India because the: [2015]
o: (a) Lok Sabha is elected directly by the people
(d) Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The defining feature of a parliamentary system is the executive's (Council of Ministers) collective responsibility to the legislature (Lok Sabha).

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Rajya Sabha and Money Bills: 1️⃣ The Rajya Sabha has no power either to reject or to amend a Money Bill 2️⃣ The Rajya Sabha cannot vote on the Demands for Grants 3️⃣ The Rajya Sabha cannot discuss the Annual Financial Statement. [2015]
questions.e: The RS cannot reject/amend Money Bills or vote on Demands for Grants. However, it is fully empowered to discuss the Annual Financial Statement (Budget).

questions.q: When a bill is referred to a joint sitting of both the Houses of the Parliament, it has to be passed by: [2015]
o: (b) three-fourths majority of members present and voting
(a) a simple majority of members present and voting
questions.e: Under Article 108, a bill in a joint sitting is passed if approved by a simple majority of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Executive Power of the Union of India is vested in the Prime Minister 2️⃣ The Prime Minister is the ex officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board. [2015]
questions.e: Executive power is vested in the President. The Cabinet Secretary, not the Prime Minister, is the ex-officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board.

questions.q: Democracy's superior virtue lies in the fact that it calls into activity: [2017]
o: (c) a superior individual with dynamism and vision
(b) the methods for strengthening executive leadership
(d) a band of dedicated party workers
(a) the intelligence and character of ordinary men and women
questions.e: Democracy relies on the consent and decision-making of the people, which in turn calls upon the intelligence and character of ordinary citizens.

questions.q: One of the implications of equality in society is the absence of: [2017]
questions.e: A primary step toward equality is ending formal systems of inequality and special privileges that restrict positions or rights to specific groups.

questions.q: Which of the following are not necessarily the consequences of the proclamation of the President's rule in a State? 1️⃣ Dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly 2️⃣ Removal of the Council of Ministers 3️⃣ Dissolution of the local bodies. [2017]
questions.e: President's rule necessitates the removal of the Council of Ministers. However, the Assembly can be suspended rather than dissolved, and local bodies are not automatically dissolved.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of Indian federalism? [2017]
o: (c) The federating units have been given unequal representation in the Rajya Sabha
(d) It is the result of an agreement among the federating units
(a) There is an independent judiciary in India
(b) Powers have been clearly divided between the Centre and the States
questions.e: Unlike the US, the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement between states; states have no right to secede from the union.

questions.q: Local self-government can be best explained as an exercise in: [2017]
questions.e: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended local self-government (Panchayati Raj) as a means of achieving "democratic decentralization."

questions.q: The main advantage of the parliamentary form of government is that: [2017]
o: (a) the executive and legislature work independently
(d) the head of the government cannot be changed without election
(b) it provides continuity of policy and is more efficient
(c) the executive remains responsible to the legislature
questions.e: The hallmark of parliamentary democracy is the collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature.

questions.q: Out of the following statements, choose the one that brings out the principle underlying the Cabinet form of Government: [2017]
o: (b) A mechanism for speeding up activities
(d) A device for strengthening the hands of the he...
(c) A mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ens...
questions.e: The Cabinet form of government is a mechanism designed to ensure the collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature and, by extension, the people.

questions.q: The Parliament of India exercises control over the functions of the Council of Ministers through: 1️⃣ Adjournment motion 2️⃣ Question hour 3️⃣ Supplementary questions. [2017]
questions.e: Parliament uses various devices like Question Hour (where supplementary questions are asked) and motions (like Adjournment or No-Confidence) to hold ministers accountable.

questions.q: With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A private member's bill is a bill presented by a nominated MP 2️⃣ Recently, a private member's bill has been passed in Parliament for the first time in history. [2017]
questions.e: A private member's bill is introduced by any MP who is not a minister. Fourteen such bills have been passed in Indian history, so neither statement is correct.

questions.q: For election to the Lok Sabha, a nomination paper can be filed by: [2017]
o: (c) any citizen of India whose name appears in the electoral roll of a constituency
(b) a resident of the constituency from which the election is to be contested
questions.e: Any Indian citizen whose name is registered in an electoral roll (in any constituency) can file a nomination for the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In the election for Lok Sabha, the winning candidate must get at least 50 per cent of the votes 2️⃣ In Lok Sabha, the Speaker's post goes to the majority party and the Deputy Speaker's to the Opposition. [2017]
questions.e: India uses the "First Past the Post" system where a winner doesn't need 50%. The division of Speaker/Deputy Speaker posts is an informal consensus, not a constitutional provision.

questions.q: Right to vote and to be elected in India is a: [2017]
questions.e: Article 326 of the Constitution guarantees the right to vote to every adult citizen, making it a Constitutional Right.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Election Commission of India is a five-member body 2️⃣ Union Ministry of Home Affairs decides the election schedule 3️⃣ Election Commission resolves disputes relating to splits/mergers of recognized parties. [2017]
questions.e: The EC is a three-member body (not five). The EC itself (not MHA) decides the election schedule. Resolving split/merger disputes is a function of the EC.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the first Lok Sabha: 1️⃣ The single largest party in the opposition was the Swatantra Party 2️⃣ A "Leader of the Opposition" was recognized for the first time in 1969 3️⃣ A party must have minimum 75 members to have a recognized LoP. [2018]
questions.e: In the first LS, the Communist Party of India (16 seats) was the largest opposition, not Swatantra. The LoP was first recognized in 1969. The required strength is 10% (55 members), not 75.

questions.q: Which Parliamentary Committee scrutinizes whether executive rules are within the scope of delegation? [2018]
questions.e: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation ensures that the powers to make rules and regulations delegated by Parliament or the Constitution are being properly exercised by the Executive.

questions.q: Regarding Money Bill, which of the following statements is not correct? [2018]
o: (d) A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money
(c) A Money Bill is concerned with the appropriation of moneys out of the Contingency Fund of India
(b) A Money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund
(a) A bill is a Money Bill if it contains provisions for imposition or regulation of any tax
questions.e: Article 110 relates to the Consolidated Fund of India. While the custody of the Contingency Fund is mentioned, standard interpretation and UPSC key identify statement (c) as the incorrect one in the context of Money Bill definitions.

questions.q: With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following: 1️⃣ The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State 2️⃣ The value of the vote of MPs of the Lok Sabha is more than the value of the vote of MPs of the Rajya Sabha. [2018]
questions.e: MLA vote value depends on state population, so it varies. However, the value of an MP's vote is uniform (708 at the time) regardless of which House they belong to.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly shall vacate office if he/she ceases to be a member 2️⃣ Whenever the Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall vacate office immediately. [2018]
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. However, Article 179 provides that the Speaker remains in office after dissolution until just before the first meeting of the new Assembly.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ No criminal proceedings shall be instituted against the Governor during his term 2️⃣ The emoluments of the Governor shall not be diminished during his term. [2018]
questions.e: Governors enjoy personal immunity from criminal proceedings during their term. Their emoluments and allowances also cannot be reduced while they are in office.

questions.q: If the President exercises power under Article 356 in a particular State: [2018]
o: (a) the Assembly of the State is automatically dissolved
(c) Article 19 is suspended in that State
(b) the powers of the Legislature of that State shall be exercisable by Parliament
(d) the President can make laws relating to that State
questions.e: Under Article 356 (President's Rule), the President can declare that the powers of the state legislature will be exercised by or under the authority of Parliament.

questions.q: The Ninth Schedule was introduced in the Constitution during the prime ministership of: [2019]
questions.e: The Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951, which occurred during the tenure of Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 exempts several posts from 'Office of Profit' 2️⃣ The Act was amended five times 3️⃣ The term 'Office of Profit' is well-defined in the Constitution. [2019]
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; the term 'Office of Profit' is not defined in the Constitution of India.

questions.q: With reference to the Legislative Assembly of a state, consider the following: 1️⃣ The Governor makes a customary address at the first session of the year 2️⃣ When a State Legislature does not have a rule on a matter, it follows the Lok Sabha rule. [2019]
questions.e: Both statements are considered correct by the official UPSC key. The Governor's address is mandatory, and in the absence of specific state rules, Lok Sabha procedures are typically followed.

questions.q: Which commission/committee suggested the Governor should be a detached figure from outside the state? [2019]
o: (d) National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution
questions.e: The Sarkaria Commission (1983) recommended that the Governor should be an eminent person from outside the state without intense political links.

questions.q: In India, which of the following review the independent regulators in sectors like telecommunications, insurance, etc.? 1️⃣ Ad Hoc Committees set up by Parliament 2️⃣ Parliamentary Department Related Standing Committees 3️⃣ Finance Commission 4️⃣ Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission 5️⃣ NITI Aayog. [2019]
questions.e: Independent regulators are reviewed by Parliamentary Committees (Ad Hoc and Standing). NITI Aayog and the Finance Commission do not have this mandate.

questions.q: In the context of polity, which one of the following is the most appropriate definition of liberty? [2019]
o: (c) Opportunity to do whatever one likes
(a) Protection against the tyranny of political rulers
questions.e: While historically liberty meant absence of restraint, the modern and most appropriate definition (per UPSC) is the positive concept: the opportunity to develop one's personality fully.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the characteristic appropriate for bureaucracy in India? [2020]
o: (b) An agency for strengthening the structure of federalism
(d) An agency for the implementation of public policy
(c) An agency for facilitating political stability and economic growth
(a) An agency widening the scope of parliamentary democracy
questions.e: Bureaucrats are appointed to implement the public policies determined by the government of the day.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ According to the Constitution, a person eligible to vote can be made a minister in a state for six months even if not a member 2️⃣ According to RPA 1951, a person convicted and sentenced to 5 years is permanently disqualified. [2020]
questions.e: A non-member can be a minister for 6 months (though they must meet age criteria, which varies from voting age). Statement 2 is wrong because disqualification is for 6 years after release, not permanent.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The President can summon a session of Parliament at such place as he/she thinks fit 2️⃣ The Constitution provides for three sessions but it is not mandatory 3️⃣ There is no minimum number of days the Parliament must meet. [2020]
questions.e: Under Article 85, the President chooses the time and place. The Constitution does not specify three sessions or a minimum number of days, though the gap between sessions cannot exceed 6 months.

questions.q: Rajya Sabha has equal powers with Lok Sabha in: [2020]
o: (a) The matter of creating new all India services
questions.e: Under Article 368, both Houses have equal power regarding Constitution Amendment Bills. In contrast, RS has special powers for All India Services and no power over cut motions or government removal.

questions.q: A constitutional government by definition is a: [2020]
questions.e: A constitutional government is one where state authority is limited by law (specifically fundamental rights) to protect individual citizens.

questions.q: If the RBI decides to adopt an expansionist monetary policy, which of the following would it not do? 1️⃣ Cut and optimize the Statutory Liquidity Ratio 2️⃣ Increase the Marginal Standing Facility Rate 3️⃣ Cut the Bank Rate and Repo Rate. [2020]
questions.e: Expansionist policy involves increasing money supply. Cutting SLR, Bank Rate, and Repo Rate helps this. Increasing the MSF rate makes loans costlier and would NOT be done during expansion.

questions.q: In what way does the Lok Sabha Speaker's position differ during prorogation versus adjournment? [2004]
o: (d) The President adjourns the house sine die
(b) Only the President can summon the House after prorogation
(a) Only the Speaker can summon the House after prorogation
(c) The Speaker's term ends on prorogation
questions.e: The Speaker can adjourn the House (temporarily stop the sitting), but once the House is prorogued (session ended), only the President has the power to summon it back.

questions.q: What is the requirement for a no-confidence motion to be admitted in the Lok Sabha? [2014]
questions.e: According to Rule 198 of the Lok Sabha, a motion of no-confidence needs the support of at least 50 members for its introduction.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about the removal of the Vice-President? [2004]
o: (c) Can be removed by the President at will
(d) Requires a joint sitting of Parliament
(a) Requires a simple majority in Lok Sabha
(b) Must be initiated in the Rajya Sabha by an absolute majority
questions.e: Article 67(b) specifies that the VP is removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all then members (absolute majority) and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Under the Order of Precedence, where does the Chief Justice of India rank compared to a Cabinet Minister? [2000]
questions.e: The Chief Justice of India ranks higher (position 6) than Union Cabinet Ministers (position 7) in the official Order of Precedence.

questions.q: The "Panchsheel" principles were established between which two countries? [1997]
questions.e: The Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) were formed in 1954 as a series of agreements between India and the People's Republic of China.

questions.q: What happens if the Lok Sabha is dissolved regarding the office of the Speaker? [2004]
o: (c) The Speaker continues until the first meeting of the new House
(d) The President takes over Speaker's duties
questions.e: Under the Constitution, the Speaker does not vacate office on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha but continues until immediately before the first meeting of the new House.

questions.q: Which body is responsible for providing secretarial assistance to Cabinet Committees? [2014]
questions.e: The Cabinet Secretariat is responsible for providing secretarial assistance to Cabinet Committees and preparing the agenda for Cabinet meetings.
